Chelsey Hockett

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 5, Dallas County, Texas · Challenger

Stay-at-home parent and community organizer. She previously worked in restaurants and for an airline.

Chelsey Hockett is a Democrat from Terrell, Texas, and this is her first run for office. She describes herself as a mother of two from a union family. She finished first in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for Texas's 5th Congressional District with 46.3%, then beat Ruth Torres in the May 26, 2026 runoff with about 53% to win the Democratic nomination against incumbent Republican Lance Gooden.

Where Hockett stands

Health care
Supports Medicare for All. She calls health care a human right and says a universal system would eliminate insurance premiums and deductibles.
Minimum wage and Social Security
Proposes a $25 federal minimum wage tied to cost of living. Supports a $200 increase in Social Security benefits, paid for by removing the cap on the Social Security payroll tax.
Tariffs and cost of living
Supports ending President Trump's tariffs, saying they raise consumer prices. Also supports universal childcare and building more affordable housing.
Labor
Supports passing the PRO Act to protect workers' right to organize, unionize and bargain without retaliation.
Taxes
Supports closing tax loopholes, a progressive income tax and a wealth tax on corporations and the ultra-wealthy.
Education
Supports full federal funding for public schools and higher teacher pay. Opposes school vouchers, which she says take money from public schools.
Immigration
Supports abolishing ICE and replacing it with what she calls humane, accountable immigration services. Supports pathways to citizenship, which she argues would do more for border security.
Abortion
Supports codifying Roe v. Wade, saying a woman's health decisions belong to her, her doctor and her conscience.
Elections and ethics
Supports the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and a ban on partisan gerrymandering. Supports banning insider trading by members of Congress and limiting corporate and billionaire money in politics.
Energy and environment
Supports a Green New Deal to expand renewable energy and a moratorium on AI data centers, citing their water use and pollution.

Background

  • Has not held elected office; first-time candidate
  • Democratic nominee for U.S. House, TX-5 (won May 26, 2026 runoff over Ruth Torres, about 53%–47%)
  • March 3, 2026 Democratic primary: first place with 46.3%
  • Bachelor's degree, Texas Woman's University (2015)
  • High school: Marcus High School
  • Former restaurant and airline worker; former retail store general manager, according to a campaign-site summary
  • Active with the Kaufman County Democratic Party
  • Endorsed by the Texas AFL-CIO and Stonewall Democrats of Dallas
